title: Data Modeling and Residuals
summary: Tilt and shift a line over eight delivery routes and watch the residual plot decide whether a straight line is the right model.
narration: Every model misses. In this chapter you fit straight lines to real data, then look hard at what each line got wrong. Slide the line over a courier's eight delivery routes, watch the leftover gaps shrink, and read the pattern they make. A small total is not enough, because the shape of the residuals is what tells you whether a straight line was ever the right idea.

practice.prompt: The line y = 3x + 7 is used to model three delivery routes, given as (packages, minutes): (2, 14), (4, 20), and (6, 24). What is the sum of the squared residuals?
practice.explanation: Predictions: 3(2) + 7 = 13, 3(4) + 7 = 19, 3(6) + 7 = 25. Residuals are observed minus predicted: 14 - 13 = 1, 20 - 19 = 1, 24 - 25 = -1. Squaring and adding gives 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

practice.prompt: A least-squares model for a seedling's height in centimeters after x weeks is y = 2.4x + 6. At week 7 the seedling measures 21.6 cm. What is the residual, in centimeters?
practice.explanation: The model predicts 2.4(7) + 6 = 16.8 + 6 = 22.8 cm. Residual = observed - predicted = 21.6 - 22.8 = -1.2 cm, so the seedling is 1.2 cm shorter than predicted.

practice.prompt: A straight-line model is fitted to 12 data points. Its sum of squared residuals is 40, and its residual plot rises at both ends and dips in the middle. What does that residual plot tell you?
choices: Some other straight line would give a smaller squared total.
The relationship is not linear, so a curved model would fit better.
The data contain exactly one outlier.
Nothing; only the size of the squared total matters.
practice.explanation: A U-shaped residual plot is left-over structure: after a straight line is subtracted, the ends still sit above it and the middle below, which is exactly what a curve looks like. It does not mean the line is not least-squares, since the least-squares line of curved data shows the same U — the squared total is already as small as any straight line can make it, and the U is still there. One outlier would be a single stray residual, not a smooth U across all 12. And the total alone is not the whole story: 40 could come from a good fit or a wrong model, so the shape of the residuals matters too.
